answer_text: The defensible, KG-supported mechanism is: DNA damage / replication stress → activation of sensor kinases ATM and ATR (KG: ATM/ATR → G2/M DNA-damage/replication-stress pathway edges) → engagement of G2/M DNA damage checkpoint pathway node (KG) → activation/engagement of TP53 → induction of pro‑apoptotic effectors PUMA and NOXA and TP53-related COP1 regulation (KG). Notes/limits: reported CHEK1 edges are contested and other canonical transducers/effectors (CHK2, CDC25s, CDKs, CDKN1A/p21, WEE1, RB1) are not consistently present in this KG fragment and therefore are not asserted as part of the KG-derived mechanism; XRCC4/5/6 and HMGA1 appear in the KG but map to a distinct '2‑LTR circle formation' pathway and are not shown here to mediate checkpoint activation. TP53 is also shown as linked to small‑molecule compounds in the KG, supporting druggability but not altering the mechanistic chain above.
